title: Imperial Envoys Have Arrived
next_chapter_hook: The Imperial envoy revealed a shocking secret: Chen Nian's disappearance was no accident, but a crucial step in the Heavenly Eye's plot spanning a hundred years—she is the sole key to opening the Heavenly Fate Treasury.

text.content: That familiar face made Chen Ji's pupils contract sharply. The betrayer's outline gradually clarified in the candlelight—it was A Fu, the servant who had followed him for years, now quietly slipping forged evidence into his clothes. Rage surged in his chest like magma, yet before he could speak, hurried footsteps sounded outside the door. "Chen Ji, Servant Disciple of Tianqing Sect, the Imperial Special Envoy has arrived—you have the time of one incense stick to present yourself at the Council Hall!" Chen Ji slowly closed his eyes, forcing the killing intent that threatened to burst forth back into his belly. The most dangerous variable in a chess game was never the enemy, but betrayal by those you trusted most—he would remember this.

Inside the Council Hall, the atmosphere was so tense it could be wrung like water. Three envoys in玄金蟒袍 robes sat dignified at the head, their masked gazes sweeping across the assembly like examining ants. The leader idly toyed with a Jade Slip, his voice cold: "Chen Ji, Servant Disciple of Tianqing Sect, entered at fourteen, made zero progress in ten years... interesting." He pivoted abruptly, "This envoy comes by order of the Heavenly Fate Pavilion to investigate a treasure lost for a century—the Tianji Record." At these words, murmurs erupted in the hall. Sect Master Ling Yuan's expression changed drastically, a fleeting terror flickering in his eyes.

dialogue.content: "You needn't be nervous. This envoy hasn't come to interrogate." The Imperial envoy rose slowly, his玄金蟒袍 robes gleaming with a cold, ethereal light in the Spiritual Energy. "Quite the opposite—the Imperial Court is willing to grant you an opportunity to rise to greatness. The Tianji Record recognizing its master—we already know. We simply didn't expect it to choose atrash." He sneered, his tone full of amusement. "But this actually saves considerable trouble. Atrash is controllable, atrash is obedient, atrash... easy to manipulate."

text.content: Chen Ji stood in the hall's center, shoulders trembling slightly—that was the expression of fear. Everyone in the hall thought so, even Su Qingyao's brow creasing further. Yet no one saw the subtle curve forming on his lowered face. Atrash is easy to manipulate? Heh, let me show you just how big a wave thistrash can make. He raised his head, eyes full of panic: "My lord... I-I truly don't know what the Tianji Record is..."

choice.prompt: The Imperial envoy extended a token emanating cold, eerie energy, claiming that if Chen Ji would "submit", he could gain entry to the Imperial Court's core. How should Chen Ji respond to this sudden "olive branch"?

choices.description: Outwardly appear overwhelmed with gratitude, accepting the Imperial Court's recruitment while secretly harboring other plans
choices.visible_reward: Gain Imperial Court status and access to higher-level intelligence
choices.risk_hint: The Imperial Court's intentions are unclear; may be used as a pawn to be consumed

text.content: Chen Ji's hands trembled slightly as he accepted the token, his terrified, uneasy appearance causing the Imperial envoy to nod with satisfaction. "A wise man knows when to bow to reality," the envoy smiled. "In three days, come with this envoy to the capital." As he turned to leave, Chen Ji lowered his head, a cold light flashing in his eyes—using the situation to enter the game was precisely his intention. The moment the token entered his hand, an icy divine sense quietly scanned the depths of his Mental Sea, as if confirming something. Chen Ji's heart tightened, but his expression grew even more deferential.

choices.text: Politely decline to advance by retreating
choices.description: Refuse using the excuse of knowing histrash status, appearing even more cowardly to make the other party lower their guard
choices.risk_hint: The envoy may be humiliated and fly into rage, applying pressure on the spot

text.content: "Your lordship honors me too much..." Chen Ji thudded to his knees, his voice trembling violently. "But I'm merely atrash who hasn't even achieved Foundation Building—how dare I aspire to the Imperial Court? I-I only wish to sweep floors in the sect and live out my remaining years..." He kowtowed repeatedly, acting the coward to perfection. The envoy's brow creased slightly, a flash of displeasure in his gaze: "Interesting. This envoy has never seen someone refuse such an opportunity." He clasped his hands behind his back. "Very well, this matter isn't urgent. Consider it carefully." Though his tone was light, there was considerably more scrutiny in it.

choices.description: Pretend to be tempted but have reservations, testing what price the Imperial Court is willing to pay
choices.visible_cost: Expose that one has ulterior motives
choices.visible_reward: Obtain more intelligence about the Imperial Court's plans
choices.risk_hint: If conditions are too excessive, one's disguise may be seen through

text.content: Chen Ji wore a conflicted expression, hesitating for a long moment before whispering: "My lord... I don't seek glory, only... only to preserve my life. Since the Tianji Record chose me, I live in fear every day..." He raised his head, eyes full of plea. "Can the Imperial Court protect me?" The envoy laughed heartily: "Imperial protection? Who in this world would dare move against someone the Heavenly Fate Pavilion has set its eyes upon?" His tone shifted. "However, if you want to know more... you'll need to show some sincerity first."

When the envoy saw Chen Ji's attitude soften, he took out a yellowed scroll from his sleeve and slowly unrolled it. The figure in the painting was elegant and refined, with features surprisingly similar to Chen Ji's own. "This man is named Chen Xuan, the previous master of the Tianji Record," the envoy's voice suddenly dropped. "A century ago, he was the guardian of the Tianji Record and also... the Imperial Court's appointed Imperial Preceptor. However, he betrayed the Pavilion of Heavenly Secrets, stole what should not have been stolen, and was ultimately executed. He looked meaningfully at Chen Ji. "Interestingly, his surname is the same as yours."

dialogue.content: "Do you think the Imperial Court seeks the Tianji Record for what?" The envoysneered一声，said coldly, putting away the scroll. "Let me tell you, the Tianji Record is merely one of the keys to opening that door. The true treasure is the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key'—a divine object capable of rewriting the laws of heaven and reversing destiny. A century ago, Chen Xuan was executed precisely because he attempted to lay hands on this forbidden artifact."

text.content: Silence fell over the hall like death. Chen Ji's heart lurched violently, yet his face remained an expression of bewildered helplessness. Heavenly Fate Lock Key... rewriting the laws of heaven... This information was like keys unlocking sealed doors within his mind. Mr. Mo had once said—the more complete the Tianji Record, the stronger the fatal backlash of fate. Could all of this point to the same secret? He lowered his head, fingernails digging deep into his palms, forcing himself to remain calm. How much did the Imperial Court know? What were they searching for?

choice.prompt: The Imperial Court's envoy suddenly shifted topics, mentioning that the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key' plan required a special 'vessel'—someone with a bloodline connection to the Tianji Record's master. This made Chen Ji think of his sister Chen Nian, who had been missing for years. How should he respond to this sudden shock?

choices.text: Forcefully suppress emotions and maintain composure
choices.description: Bury the shock deep in his heart, letting nothing show on his surface, then secretly investigate later
choices.visible_reward: Do not expose weaknesses, do not arouse Imperial Court vigilance
choices.risk_hint: If emotional management fails, one may be detected

text.content: Chen Ji felt as if all the blood in his body was flowing backward, his fingertips almost crushed by his own grip. Chen Nian... The Imperial Court was searching for Chen Nian? It took immense willpower to suppress the overwhelming killing intent, his face instead showing confusion. "Vessel? Bloodline connection? This humble one truly does not understand what the noble lord means..." His voice was terrifyingly steady, so steady even he felt it was foreign. The envoy's gaze lingered on his face for a moment, seemingly searching for something, but finally just smiled faintly. "Don't understand? No matter, you will naturally understand in time."

choices.text: Seize the opportunity to extract more intelligence
choices.description: Pretend to be curious and inquire about the 'vessel,' attempting to obtain more information about Chen Nian's whereabouts
choices.visible_cost: May expose one's concern for the 'vessel'
choices.visible_reward: Obtain more details about the Heavenly Fate Lock Key
choices.risk_hint: Asking too many questions may arouse suspicion

text.content: "The noble lord mentioned the vessel..." Chen Ji spoke cautiously, his eyes filled with curiosity rather than fear. "What is it? What connection does it have with the Tianji Record?" The envoy raised an eyebrow, seemingly surprised by his "eagerness to learn," but still patiently explained: "The Heavenly Fate Lock Key requires special bloodline to be its vessel. Chen Xuan divided the key into two halves back then—one hidden within the Tianji Record, the other..." He deliberately paused, observing Chen Ji's reaction. "He secretly sent it away, hiding it somewhere."

"Before Chen Xuan was executed, he left behind final words—'Heaven has its constants, the lock key does not perish; when one with destiny appears in the mortal world.'" The envoy paced with hands behind his back, his tone carrying a hint of mockery. "For a hundred years, the Imperial Court has been searching for that 'person of destiny.' The Tianji Record chose you, and your bloodline... Heh heh, perhaps can help us find the other half of the key." He turned to face Chen Ji directly. "So, are you willing to cooperate? Cooperate well, and you shall have wealth and honor; cooperate poorly..." He did not finish, but the unspoken implication caused the temperature in the hall to plummet several degrees.

dialogue.content: At this moment, a weak and urgent voice transmitted through Chen Ji's Mental Sea from Mr. Mo: "Boy, steady yourself! Behind the Imperial Court stands the Eye of Heavenly Law—it is testing you! Chen Xuan's dying words were tampered with—the original saying was 'Heaven's fate is impermanent, the lock key does not perish,' not 'has constants'! They need your bloodline to activate the Tianji Record, but under no circumstances can the complete Tianji Record fall into their hands!" Mr. Mo's voice grew fainter. "Remember, your sister... She was taken by the Eye of Heavenly Law..." The words abruptly cut off, as if severed by some powerful force.

text.content: Chen Ji's pupils contracted slightly, his heart churning like a mighty storm. The Eye of Heavenly Law... So the Imperial Court was merely its chess piece! Chen Nian's disappearance, being taken by the Holy Sect... Behind all of this lay such an enormous hidden hand manipulating everything? He felt suffocated, as if an invisible hand was reaching toward him from the Void, ready to crush him along with the entire chess game. But he could not panic, not now at least. He drew a deep breath, pressing all emotions into the abyss. When he raised his head again, it was once more that harmless expression of a useless wretch.

choice.prompt: The Imperial Court's envoy delivered his final ultimatum: within three days, either accompany the envoy group to the capital to receive "protection," or be considered a fugitive and hunted down. Facing this multiple-choice question, how should Chen Ji decide?

choices.text: Pretend to comply, accompany the envoy group to the capital
choices.description: Enter the tiger's den to investigate the Imperial Court and the Eye of Heavenly Law, but the danger is extreme
choices.visible_cost: Enter the enemy's lair, losing all support
choices.visible_reward: Access core secrets, possibly find clues about Chen Nian
choices.risk_hint: If exposed in the capital, death is certain

text.content: "Y-Your servant is willing!" Chen Ji dropped to his knees with a violent tremor in his voice, "Your servant is willing to follow the great lord to the capital!" The envoy nodded with satisfaction, "Knowing when to submit." He turned and left, leaving Chen Ji kneeling on the ground. When the hall was empty, Chen Ji slowly stood up, the fear in his expression ebbing away like a tide, replaced by bone-deep coldness and calculation. Going deeper into the capital might help him find Chen Nian. But more importantly... he wanted to see for himself what this so-called Eye of Heavenly Providence truly was.

choices.text: "Requesting a few more days to prepare"
choices.description: "Using the excuse of sorting out personal affairs to buy time, secretly contacting Su Qingyao and Ye Qing"
choices.visible_reward: "Would have time to pass messages and make arrangements"
choices.risk_hint: "The envoy may refuse, or even strengthen surveillance"

text.content: "My lord..." Chen Ji showed difficulty on his face, "Your servant still has some belongings to hand over at the sect. Could you grant a delay of three days?" The envoy frowned slightly, studied him for a moment, then snorted coldly: "In three days, I want to see you appear outside the sect gate. If you dare play tricks..." He pointed a finger, a streak of golden light entering Chen Ji's brow center—a tracking prohibition, "You should know the consequences." After the envoy left, Chen Ji dared to heave a long sigh. Three days would be enough. He had to inform Su Qingyao and Ye Qing that the Imperial Court had the Eye of Heavenly Providence behind them—this intelligence was more important than anything else.

choices.description: "Declare rather to die than betray Tianqing Sect,以此换取使者的暂时退让"

text.content: Chen Ji gritted his teeth, as if making a great decision: "My lord, forgive my offense, but though this one is useless, I cannot abandon the sect's kindness of sheltering me for over a decade!" His voice trembled, yet carried a hint of resolve. The envoy's expression darkened, about to flare up, when Sect Master Ling Yuan suddenly spoke: "Please calm your anger, honored envoy. Since this boy is a disciple of Tianqing Sect, how he is dealt with should be decided by me." Two forces clashed in the hall, Chen Ji lowered his head, cold sweat soaking through.借刀杀人? No, what was old fox Ling Yuan scheming?

After the Imperial Court envoy left, only Chen Ji and Ling Yuan remained in the hall. The old sect master's complex gaze fell upon him, and after a long while he sighed: "Chen Ji, do you know that your response today will determine the fate of Tianqing Sect?" Chen Ji kept his head bowed, yet his heart was churning with immense waves. Ling Yuan continued: "The Imperial Court... is not as simple as it appears. The person behind them has been laying plans for hundreds of years. You possess the Tianji Record, have Chen Xuan's bloodline, and also..." He suddenly paused, as if hesitating. "And also what?" Chen Ji pressed. Ling Yuan shook his head: "It's still too early to say. You only need to remember one thing—your sister is alive, and she's waiting for you."

dialogue.content: The old sect master turned to leave, but stopped at the door, speaking without turning back: "In three days, if you leave with the Imperial Court envoy, I'll pretend I never had you as a disciple. If you stay..." An uncommon warmth crept into his aged voice, "Though Tianqing Sect is small, it is not a place where others can slaughter at will." The hall doors closed, Chen Ji stood alone in the empty Council Hall, when a warm jade pendant appeared in his hand—when had that gotten there? It was what Ling Yuan had quietly left behind. He turned the jade pendant over, and on the back were carved two archaic characters: "Chen Nian."

text.content: Chen Ji stared at the jade pendant until his knuckles turned white from gripping. Chen Nian... his sister was alive! How did Ling Yuan have her token? What was his connection to his sister's disappearance? A barrage of questions exploded in his mind, but reason told him this was not the time to pursue answers. The Imperial Court envoy was still waiting outside the sect, and the three-day deadline would pass in an instant. He had to make a choice—venture into the tiger's den at great risk, or stay in the sect to watch and wait? Either way meant he would have to face that terrifying existence that had been plotting for centuries head-on. In the flickering candlelight, Chen Ji slowly tightened his grip on the jade pendant, a decisive glint flashing in his eyes. The chess game had changed, but he never feared variables—he only feared the variables wouldn't be interesting enough.

Suddenly, footsteps came from outside the hall. Su Qingyao's figure appeared at the entrance. Her expression was grave; she had clearly heard about the Imperial Court envoy's visit. Their eyes met, and Chen Ji saw worry, confusion, and an indescribable complexity in her gaze. "Chen Ji," she spoke, her voice softer than usual, "who exactly are you?" This question was like a blade, piercing straight into Chen Ji's heart. He opened his mouth, wanting to explain, but found thousands of words stuck in his throat. Su Qingyao stepped closer, "Whoever you are, I only want to know one thing—will you harm Tianqing Sect?" Her eyes blazed, gazing into Chen Ji's very soul, as if trying to see through him.

Chen Ji looked at this woman who had always tried to uncover his secrets, and suddenly smiled. That smile carried bitterness, relief, but mostly a desperate resolve. "No." His voice was soft, yet every word was clear, "Tianqing Sect is my only retreat. I want it to endure more than anyone." Su Qingyao stared at him for a long time before finally nodding lightly. "Good." She turned to leave, pausing at the threshold to leave behind a sentence: "In three days, wherever you go, I will follow. This is... the duty of the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow." Her figure vanished into the night, yet Chen Ji stood there for a long while, gazing toward where she had disappeared, an unnamed emotion surging in his heart. Someone was willing to stand by his side in the darkness—even with thorns carpeting the path ahead, what was there to fear?

Deep into the night, Chen Ji sat alone in the crude Servants' Quarters, pressing the jade pendant inscribed with "Chen Nian" against his forehead. The Tianji Record Fragment silently emerged, and Master Mo'sweak的声音再次响起: "Boy, you did well. The Imperial Court envoy has taken the aura of the Tianji Record Fragment. Within three days, they cannot track your exact location." Chen Ji opened his eyes: "Master, the Imperial Court has the Eye of Heavenly Providence behind them—you knew this all along, didn't you?" Master Mo沉默片刻: "I know some, but not everything. The more complete the Tianji Record, the more I can perceive." He paused, "Boy, your sister Chen Nian is indeed the core of the Heavenly Fate Lock Key plan. The Eye of Heavenly Providence needs her to open some kind of forbidden thing... and the Tianji Record you carry is the only thing that can stop it."

Chen Ji slowly tucked the jade pendant into his chest, stood up, and walked to the window. Moonlight flowed like water, sprinkling across his serene features, betraying no emotion whatsoever. Imperial Court, Eye of Heavenly Providence, Heavenly Fate Lock Key, Chen Nian... all the clues converged at this moment, sketching out an enormous chess game he had never imagined. And he, once deemedtrash by everyone, had unknowingly become the most crucial piece on the board. But so what if he was a piece? The game was vast, yet a move must eventually be made. He, Chen Ji, never believed in fate—if fate dared to oppose him, he would trample fate beneath his feet. In the distance, the Imperial Court envoy's carriage slowly traveled through the night, and within the carriage's curtains, the envoy's gaze pierced through the darkness, seemingly able to see Chen Ji's direction. "An interesting little thing..." he murmured softly, "I hope you can bring us a pleasant surprise."
